history.period: 875-876 CE (CONFLICT: sources cite both years - verify)
history.summary: Chaturbhuj Temple is a rock-cut monolithic Hindu temple carved from a single rock face on the eastern road inside Gwalior Fort. Its sanctum inscription records that it was built by Alla, son of Vaillabhatta and grandson of Nagarabhatta, during the Gurjara-Pratihara period (inscription dated 876 CE; popular sources often say 875 CE). It is dedicated to the four-armed (Chaturbhuj) form of Lord Vishnu, whose idol stands in the sanctum though its face is defaced. The temple is famous as the 'Temple of Zero' because its inscription contains one of the earliest known written uses of the numeral zero (in the number 270). It has a Nagara-style pyramidal shikhara, a portico on four carved pillars, and entrance flanked by river goddesses Ganga and Yamuna; carvings also depict Shiva and forms of Durga, reflecting the religious diversity of the 9th century.

town_description: Gwalior is a historic city in northern Madhya Pradesh, dominated by the 8th-century Gwalior Fort perched on a sandstone plateau. It was the seat of the Tomar rulers and later the Scindia dynasty, and is celebrated as the birthplace of Tansen and the Gwalior gharana of classical music. Its monuments, including the Saas-Bahu and Teli ka Mandir temples, make it one of Madhya Pradesh's foremost heritage destinations.
